Pediatric concussion patients may not always be compliant with their discharge instructions. While a significant number of pediatric patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) are mostly compliant, a substantial portion of them still report returning to the ED on the day of injury or experiencing symptoms without medical clearance.

In general, it is essential for healthcare providers to ensure that pediatric concussion patients understand and adhere to their discharge instructions. This includes:

*   Completing all necessary follow-up appointments
*   Monitoring for any signs of worsening symptoms or difficulty walking
*   Reporting any concerns or questions to the care team

Healthcare providers should work closely with pediatric concussion specialists, such as athletic trainers and emergency medicine physicians, to develop effective communication strategies for patients and their families.
